newsitem.title: INDIA: India Crisil assigns 'AAA' rating for NABARD bonds.
newsitem.headline: India Crisil assigns 'AAA' rating for NABARD bonds.

text.p: The Credit Rating Information Services of India Ltd (Crisil) said it assigned a 'AAA' rating for a bond issue of the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (Nabard), indicating highest safety with regard to timely payment of interest and principal.
Nabard was set up to providing credit for agriculture and rural development and it serves as the apex body involved in policy, planning and credit dispensation for these activities.
Crisil said Nabard has access to a large pool of National Rural Credit (NRC) funds which have been contributed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and Nabard over the last decade.
"These funds do not require any servicing in terms of interest or principal payments. Other borrowings are supported by the government and are at subsidised rates," it said.

The capital structure, with high proportion of own funds, and borrowings at subsidised rates leads to low cost of funds for Nabard. The refinancing rates of Nabard are regulated to a large extent, it said.

In spite of low yield on the advances portfolio Nabard has high internal accruals (7.6 billion rupees in 1995-96) on account of low cost of funds, exemption from income tax and no dividend payout. The capital adequacy of Nabard is favourable at 29.53 percent, Crisil said.
Nabard lends to state cooperative banks, land development banks, regional rural banks (RRB) and the commercial banks, many of which are financially weak.
